origin_narratives.title: Nachiketa asks Yama what follows death
origin_narratives.summary: In Max Muller's 1884 Katha Upanishad, Vajasravasa gives worn-out cows in sacrifice. His young son Nachiketa repeatedly asks to whom he will be given; in anger his father says, ‘to Death.’ Nachiketa reaches Yama's abode and waits three nights while Yama is absent. Yama returns and grants three boons: a calm welcome and reconciliation with his father, the fire teaching, and finally an answer to the disputed question of what follows death. Yama first offers long life, descendants, wealth, power, music and pleasure, but Nachiketa refuses what is temporary. Yama distinguishes the good from the merely pleasant and teaches about Self, knowledge, discipline and death; the text closes with Nachiketa attaining that teaching's goal. The child danger, waiting, reconciliation and fire are not actions to copy. This story proves no afterlife fact and supplies neither Sarva Pitru origin, ancestor message nor Shraddha vidhi.

origin_narratives.title: Nachiketa Yama से death के बाद का प्रश्न पूछते हैं
origin_narratives.summary: Max Muller की 1884 Katha Upanishad में Vajasravasa sacrifice में worn-out cows देते हैं। Young son Nachiketa बार-बार पूछते हैं उन्हें किसे दिया जाएगा; anger में father कहते हैं, ‘Death को।’ Nachiketa Yama के abode पहुँचकर उनकी absence में three nights wait करते हैं। Yama लौटकर three boons देते हैं: father का calm welcome/reconciliation, fire teaching, और अंत में death के बाद क्या होता है इस disputed question का answer। Yama पहले long life, descendants, wealth, power, music और pleasure offer करते हैं, पर Nachiketa temporary चीजें reject करते हैं। Yama good और merely pleasant का distinction तथा Self, knowledge, discipline और death की teaching देते हैं; text Nachiketa के teaching-goal attainment पर close होता है। Child danger, waiting, reconciliation और fire copy करने की actions नहीं। Story afterlife fact prove नहीं करती और Sarva Pitru origin, ancestor message या Shraddha vidhi नहीं देती।

variants.scope: Grief, abuse, estrangement, adoption, lineage, child/dependent, food, animal, water, fire, crowd, privacy, accessibility or cost needs
variants.difference: Safety और consent participation बदल/रोक सकते हैं और ritual completion से ऊपर हैं।

safety_and_boundaries: Fast, dehydration, medicine change, bath, river/ghat entry, fire, smoke, crowd, travel, animal feeding, food disposal, donation, recitation, purchase या priest payment required नहीं।
कोई child/dependent Nachiketa का departure, danger, fasting, waiting, abusive command, unsafe reconciliation या fire copy न करे; guardian safety story/ritual से ऊपर है।
किसी पर forgiveness, positive memory, family disclosure, belief, photograph, touch, public grief, gotra claim या unsafe relative contact owed नहीं।
Dreams, birds, animals, food, water, flame, coincidence और feelings ancestor messages नहीं।
Liberation, satisfaction, debt release, defect/curse removal, marriage, progeny, wealth, prosperity, peace या reunion guaranteed नहीं।
Gender, kinship, marriage, fertility, adoption, lineage या participation status पर shame/duty assign न करें।
Formal materials/actions यहाँ reconstruct नहीं होते; named current authority लें या private remembrance रखें।
Immediate danger में 112; medical, water, fire, animal, food, safeguarding, venue और legal rules completion से ऊपर हैं।
Authored का अर्थ यह lane है, projected, hosted, independently released या published नहीं।

open_gaps: Not projected, hosted or published; formal Shraddha, Tamil/Odia Mahalaya and named Gaya/ghat/institution procedures remain separate owner lanes.
